text: 我要说一个反直觉的结论，鸡越多，大家就越娶不起老婆。
en: I want to state a counterintuitive conclusion: the more prostitutes there are, the less able everyone is to afford a wife.

text: 首先我先说前提，不可能所有女人，甚至不可能所有年轻女人都当鸡，当鸡的肯定是一小部分，即使当鸡合法。
en: First, let me set out the premise: it is impossible for all women, or even all young women, to become prostitutes; those who do must be a small minority, even if prostitution were legal.

text: 换句话说，所有女人都有条件可以当鸡，但是并不是所有女人都会去当鸡。
en: In other words, all women are in a position to become prostitutes, but not all women will actually do so.

text: 这是这次讨论的基础前提。
en: This is the basic premise of this discussion.

text: 好了，咱们开始根据这次讨论推演。
en: Right, let us begin deducing from this discussion.

text: 假设一只鸡，每两天接一次包夜，一次500，假设其18岁开始接单，35岁太老了卖不出去，那么，其职业生涯的总收入就是17年共计6,209日（含四次润日）*500/2 =1552250,155万，咱们就算这只鸡不那么勤奋，经常不上工，只挣一百万，那么，也就是说，你的一百万可以买断这只鸡的职业生涯。
en: Suppose a prostitute takes one overnight booking every two days, at 500 each. Suppose she starts taking clients at 18 and by 35 she is too old to sell. Then her total career earnings are 17 years amounting to 6,209 days in total (including four leap days) × 500 ÷ 2 = 1,552,250, that is 1.55 million. Even if we say this prostitute is not that diligent, often does not turn up for work, and only earns one million, then that means your one million can buy out this prostitute's entire career.

text: 这时候旁边的良家坐不住了，但是你让良家去卖又不太现实，但是本质上，良家也是会选择上嫁的，就是想找个人买断自己的人生。
en: At this point the decent women nearby can no longer sit still, but it is not very realistic to expect a decent woman to sell herself. Yet essentially a decent woman will also choose to marry up; she simply wants to find someone to buy out her own life.

text: 那么问题来了，隔壁那只鸡已经把价定好了，一百万买断。
en: Then the problem arises: the prostitute next door has already set her price — one million for a full buyout.

text: 良家就靠着这个价找买主就行了。
en: The decent woman just needs to find a buyer at that price.

text: 所以才会出现彩礼这种神奇的现代风气。
en: That is why the curious modern custom of the bride price has come about.

text: 这笔钱就是良家的“人生买断费”。
en: This money is the decent woman's ‘life buyout fee’.

text: 所以独立女性这个词就很可笑，只要还想要彩礼，那就不可能独立，因为你已经把自己的人生卖了。
en: So the term ‘independent woman’ is rather laughable; as long as she still wants a bride price, she cannot possibly be independent, because she has already sold her life.

text: 至于你花了钱，能不能享受到禽类的服务，能不能真的买断，那就不在这次的讨论范围之内了。
en: As for whether, having spent the money, you can actually enjoy the services of these birds, or truly complete the buyout — that lies outside the scope of this discussion.

text: 配上这个回答咀嚼一下，风味更佳。
en: Chew on this answer alongside it for a better flavour.

text: 恶心，恶心呐
en: Disgusting, how utterly disgusting.

text: 国内分明言论很自由，这种逆天言论都能出来
en: Domestic speech is clearly very free, given that such appalling remarks can even appear.

text: 鉴于有些杠精说什么扫大街之类苦活也没有上层人去干，我再问一下，都是下层人干的活计为什么卖淫的单位收入比扫大街高很多倍呢？
en: Given that some trolls say even menial work like street sweeping is not done by people from the upper classes, let me ask again: if it is all work done by the lower classes, why is the per-unit income of prostitution many times higher than that of street sweeping?

text: 还不是因为两者对人格的践踏和损害有本质的不同，这高出的收入说白了就是对你失去人格的补偿罢了。
en: Is it not simply because the two differ essentially in how they trample upon and damage human dignity? The extra income, plainly put, is nothing but compensation for the loss of your dignity.

text: 说你是扫大街的并不算侮辱，而野鸡鸭子就是侮辱性的词汇这是为啥呢？
en: Calling you a street sweeper is not an insult, so why is ‘wild chicken and duck’ an insulting term?

text: 上层人作秀做慈善，体验生活送外卖，扫大街 ，下矿井，做各种志愿者等等多的是，还拿出来宣传显摆自己和底层打成一片，你猜他们为啥不去体验体验某些职业
en: Upper-class people put on shows of charity, deliver takeaway to experience life, sweep streets, go down mines, do all sorts of volunteering and so on — they even publicise it to show off how they mingle with the grassroots. Guess why they never go and ‘experience’ certain professions?

text: 我当年也觉得这事你情我愿没什么不好，看到一位网友问了下面的问题，瞬间开悟这东西本质是上对下系统性的压迫，而有些人啊，真的缺点良知…
en: I used to think this was a matter of mutual consent and nothing wrong with it, but after seeing a netizen ask the question below, I instantly realised that this is essentially a systemic, top-down oppression, and some people truly lack a conscience…

text: 一群人都说的什么乱七八糟，什么伦理道德，什么减少犯罪，我就特么的问一句，你见过市长千金，医院院长，老总媳妇这些上等阶级的女性(或者男性)去卖淫吗?(我指的是具有一定普遍性，特殊个例除外) 去挣这份钱的还不都是底层那些苦群众的妻女(当然不光女性，男性也比比皆是)!
en: A bunch of people are talking utter nonsense — ethics and morality, reducing crime, and so on. I just want to ask one damn thing: have you ever seen the daughters of mayors, the wives of hospital directors, or the wives of company bosses — women (or men) of the upper class — go into prostitution? (I mean with any real generality; exceptional individual cases excluded.) Is it not always the wives and daughters of the suffering lower-class masses who earn this money? (And of course it is not only women; men are everywhere too!)

text: 卖淫合法会让强奸犯变少就是纯扯淡的结论。
en: The claim that legalising prostitution would reduce the number of rapists is pure nonsense.

text: 先射箭在打靶，就跟说印度犯罪率很低一样搞笑，还不如说取消强奸罪直接让强奸犯清零了。
en: This is drawing the target after firing the arrow. It is as ridiculous as saying India has a very low crime rate; you might as well say abolish the crime of rape and rapists drop to zero overnight.

text: 一个是害怕轻微的治安处罚不敢去嫖而长期压抑，一个是经常嫖但钱花光了很久没碰过女人了。
en: One type is long-suppressed out of fear of minor public-order penalties and thus dares not visit prostitutes; the other frequents prostitutes but, having run out of money, has not touched a woman for a long time.

text: 哪个更可能去犯罪？
en: Which is more likely to turn to crime?

text: 古代妓院门口嚷嚷着要进去被拦下来的人，是很危险的。
en: In ancient times, the people who shouted at the brothel door demanding to be let in, only to be turned away, were dangerous.

text: 现在一样有这种人，只不过比较少也不在明处。
en: Nowadays there are still such people, only fewer and not out in the open.

text: 还有说只要管理好就不会引发犯罪。
en: There are also those who say that as long as it is well managed, it will not lead to crime.

text: 好家伙，直接把最困难的跳过是吧。
en: Good grief, you just skip right over the hardest part, do you?

text: 黄赌毒之所以限制，就是因为容易引发一系列社会治安问题而导致无法管理。
en: The reason prostitution, gambling and drugs are restricted is precisely that they easily trigger a string of public-security problems and become unmanageable.

text: 不如直接说共产主义实现了，钱和资源无限多，哪还有人犯罪，更不会有黄这个说法了。
en: You might as well just say communism has been realised, money and resources are infinite, so who would commit crime, and there would be no such thing as prostitution either.

text: 其他支持的理由，也都可以支持赌毒合法。
en: The other arguments in support could just as well support the legalisation of gambling and drugs.

text: 他们虽然一般不敢在网上说，但是他们辩解抱怨的理由也差不多
en: Although they generally dare not say it online, their reasons for arguing and complaining are much the same.

text: 一句话就能反驳呀。
en: It can be refuted in a single sentence.

text: 他说的也不存在逼迫，怎么保证？
en: He says there is no coercion either; how can that be guaranteed?

text: 国家禁止卖淫主要就是因为卖淫的背后一定有妇女拐卖和逼良为娼。
en: The state prohibits prostitution mainly because behind it there must inevitably be the trafficking of women and the forcing of decent women into prostitution.

text: 你就问他所谓的不存在逼迫怎么保证？
en: Just ask him how he guarantees this so-called absence of coercion.

text: 另外，他说的卖淫合法强奸犯罪就会下降，那他知道我们国家性犯罪的比例是多少吗？
en: Besides, he says legalising prostitution would lower rape crime — does he even know what proportion of sex crimes our country has?

text: 我们为什么要以开放卖淫来换取本来不算高的强奸犯罪的下降？
en: Why should we open up prostitution in exchange for a reduction in rape crime that is not even high to begin with?

text: 强奸犯应该打击，你是不是满足他的需求他就不做恶了。
en: Rapists should be cracked down on. Do you think that satisfying his needs means he will stop doing evil?

text: 按他的逻辑，那还有杀人犯呢，咋办？
en: By his logic, what about murderers? What then?

text: 砍人合法吗？
en: Is assault with a weapon legal?

text: 他说你反对是因为对象嫖过吗，你还给他呀，他这么支持，不就是想自己嫖吗？
en: He says you oppose it because your partner has been with a prostitute — so hand him back to her, then? He supports it so fervently precisely because he wants to go whoring himself, does he not?

text: 想还没胆，所以盼着合法化。
en: He wants to but lacks the nerve, so he longs for legalisation.

text: 这个答案从发布就不断有人上来说不合法的状态下也有拐卖人口逼良为娼，所以逻辑不对。
en: Ever since this answer was published, people have kept turning up to say that even in an illegal state there is human trafficking and the forcing of decent women into prostitution, so the logic is wrong.

text: 说这种话的人，你们是怎么好意思谈逻辑问题的？
en: People who say such things — how do you have the nerve to talk about logic?

text: 没错，即便不合法状态下也会有这些行为，但不意味着两种状态下的数量概率和难易程度是一样的呀。
en: True, even in an illegal state these behaviours exist, but that does not mean the quantity, probability and ease of it are the same under the two states.

text: 这想不明白吗？
en: Can you not grasp this?

text: 按照你们的逻辑，在杀人违法的情况下也会有杀人犯，所以杀人就该合法？
en: By your logic, since there are murderers even when murder is illegal, murder should be made legal?

text: 杀人违法就逻辑不对？
en: Is murder being illegal therefore illogical?

text: 酒驾违法的情况下也会有人喝了酒开车，所以喝酒开车就该合法？
en: When drink-driving is illegal there are still people who drink and drive, so drink-driving should be made legal?

text: 建议润去缅甸，老中就是这种禁止卖淫，吸毒和赌博的集权国家，殖批们这辈子是估计看不到改的可能性了。
en: I suggest you run off to Myanmar. China is precisely this kind of authoritarian state that bans prostitution, drug use and gambling, and you pro-Western types probably will not see any chance of it changing in your lifetime.

text: 我的建议是，支持卖淫的人去卖淫，干自己喜欢的事还能赚钱岂不美哉。
en: My suggestion is that those who support prostitution should go into prostitution themselves; doing what you love while earning money — would that not be wonderful?

text: 卧龙凤雏总是扎堆出现。
en: The sleeping dragon and the fledgling phoenix always turn up in clusters.

text: 加过一个品茶上课的老师，座驾是宝马，问干这行图啥呢，答曰来钱快，最喜欢那种聊天口嗨的，实战一分钟差不多了，最好的时候一天赚以前打工一个月的钱
en: I once added a ‘tea-savouring and tutoring’ teacher; her ride was a BMW. When I asked what she was in it for, she said the money comes fast, and she most likes the type who just talk big in chat — the actual deed lasts about a minute. At her best, she earned in a day what used to take a month of ordinary waged work.

text: 凌晨隔壁老小区里甚至会刷新under age，晚上三点出门吃烧烤就看着三五黄毛载着几个太妹有说有笑进来了，结果黄毛是最腼腆的，太妹是最疯最豪放的，有几对还谈着呢，男望风女赚钱
en: In the small hours, the old neighbourhood next door even spawns ‘under age’ minors; going out for barbecue at three in the morning, you see three or five yellow-haired lads driving in with a few delinquent girls, chatting and laughing. Yet it turns out the yellow-haired lads are the shyest, while the girls are the wildest and most uninhibited; several of the pairs are even dating — the boys keep watch while the girls earn the money.

text: 某小区还有一位出了名的，主打三块钱不带伞性价比拉满，最夸张时候门口二十来个老爷们儿在晃悠，帽子叔叔常客，被扫了又来来了又被扫，两年了坚持不懈就盯着一个小区，关键看着挺文静还挺有修养的
en: In a certain residential compound there is also a famous one whose selling point is ‘three yuan, no condom, maximum value for money’. At the most extreme, some twenty-odd men would be loitering at her door; the police are regular visitors — they sweep her up, she comes back, they sweep her up again; for two years she has persisted, fixated on one compound. The key thing is she looks quite demure and refined.

text: 可能是我眼拙，看不出她们有任何被胁迫被绑架的迹象，也看不出她们有任何不想干的样子
en: Perhaps I am unobservant, but I see no sign of them being coerced or abducted, nor any appearance of not wanting to do it.
